text: Aperture controls the amount of light entering the camera, while shutter controls the length of time the light is captured. These settings have a significant impact on exposure, depth of field, and overall image quality. Aperture determines the depth of field, with wider apertures creating a narrow depth of field and narrower apertures creating a wider depth of field. Adjusting the shutter speed allows you to control how long the light is captured, which affects exposure and can help freeze or blur motion. By adjusting the aperture and shutter speed, you can manipulate light and control the depth of field, ultimately producing images with better exposure, depth, and quality.
summary: Aperture controls light, shutter controls exposure, and settings impact depth of field, exposure, and image quality.
